author: Carlos Martinez
title: Logitech G Pro Wheel vs MOZA R5: Which Starter Wheel Setup Wins
description: Compare entry-level belt-drive and direct-drive wheels for iRacing. See which offers better value, longevity, and progression potential for your first real rig.

sections.p: Starting sim racing means choosing between technologies that feel radically different and cost roughly the same. The Logitech G Pro Wheel sits at the top of consumer-grade belt-drive design, while the MOZA R5 Bundle brings direct-drive technology to entry-level budgets. Both run around $300–400 depending on regional pricing and sales, yet they will shape your first year on track in very different ways. The choice is not which one is universally better, but which one matches your intentions: comfort and familiarity, or forward momentum into serious sim racing.

Belt-drive wheels like the Logitech G Pro deliver feedback through a system of belts and pulleys. This design softens and smooths the signal reaching your hands. Turn-in feels gentle. Curbing and bumps arrive as muted whispers rather than sharp impacts. For a first week in iRacing, this feels forgiving and encourages experimentation without sensory overload.

The MOZA R5 direct-drive system connects the motor shaft straight to the wheel hub with no mechanical filter. Every track detail arrives instantly and with full amplitude. A bump transmitted through the rim feels like a bump. Oversteer or understeer signals arrive with clarity that takes practice to interpret. Many new drivers find this precision demanding at first, but the feedback teaches racecraft faster because you cannot ignore what the car is telling you.

sections.tip: Direct-drive wheels reveal setup mistakes immediately. A belt-drive wheel may mask poor brake balance or differential tuning for weeks. If you plan to become serious about lap times, unfiltered feedback accelerates that learning curve.

sections.p: The Logitech G Pro Wheel is a proven design. It has been in production for years, parts are available, and the user base is large. The motor and electronics are reliable under normal use. Belts do wear over time and may require replacement after 3000–5000 hours of intense racing, but the cost and difficulty are manageable. For casual or part-time use, this wheel can run for years without maintenance.

MOZA direct-drive wheels carry a reputation for robust electronics and straightforward serviceability. The R5 is the entry point to that ecosystem. It uses the same motor and control architecture as more expensive MOZA models, meaning parts support exists and firmware updates are ongoing. Direct-drive elimination of belts removes a wear item entirely, though the continuous nature of the motor demands consistent power delivery and cooling.

list: Logitech G Pro: belt maintenance possible, motor reliable, wide third-party support
MOZA R5: no belts, integrated electronics, firmware-driven updates, proven motor design
Both: realistic lifespan of 5+ years at 500 hours per year for a hobbyist

sections.p: The Logitech G Pro connects via USB and works across Windows, PlayStation 5, Xbox, and even some arcade cabinets. If you ever want to race outside iRacing, this wheel opens doors. The steering wheel rim is Logitech's own design with plentiful buttons and a sturdy paddle shifter design. The ecosystem is closed: you can customize in Logitech's control panel, but you cannot swap wheels or upgrade core internals without buying a new base entirely.

MOZA R5 Bundle integrates into the MOZA ecosystem. The base accepts any quick-release MOZA wheel or aftermarket wheels designed for MOZA's standard. You can buy a CS V2 wheel later, or a CRP2 load cell pedal upgrade, or swap to an R12 when your skills demand it. The ecosystem allows growth without replacing the foundation you already own. MOZA software is Windows-only at present, and the community is smaller than Logitech's, but the upgrade path is real.

Logitech G Pro Wheel pricing (~$300–350) buys the wheel base, the included steering wheel rim, and cable only. You need pedals and a cockpit frame separately. For a true beginner rig, budget another $150–300 for load cell pedals and $200–400 for a cockpit depending on space and existing desk setup.

MOZA R5 Bundle (~$400–450 on sale) includes the wheelbase, a compact steering wheel with quick-release, and a set of load cell pedals. The pedal quality is entry-level but functional. This means a complete input setup right out of the box. If you are starting from zero, the R5 Bundle reduces initial spending and planning friction.

sections.tip: The MOZA R5 Bundle includes pedals; Logitech does not. Factor this into total rig cost before comparing prices directly. A complete pedal setup easily costs $150–300 alone.

sections.p: New drivers often find the Logitech G Pro easier on their first day. The gentler, filtered feedback feels less overwhelming. You can focus on racing lines and throttle control without interpreting complex force feedback. This builds confidence quickly and suits drivers who plan to race casually or who are new to any form of motorsport simulation.

The MOZA R5 demands more attention upfront. Stronger force feedback requires better hand position and grip technique to manage. If you are coming from a gamepad, the adjustment is noticeable. Within a week or two, most drivers adapt and begin to understand what the feedback means. Those who persist report faster skill development and a stronger connection to lap-time improvements.

Choose the Logitech G Pro Wheel if you race casually, value versatility across multiple platforms and games, want the gentlest possible entry into iRacing, or plan to race for 5–10 hours per week without future upgrades. This wheel will give you years of fun racing with minimal fuss.

Choose the MOZA R5 Bundle if you plan to race competitively, want an integrated ecosystem that supports upgrades, need pedals included in your budget, or are willing to spend the first week adapting to stronger feedback in exchange for faster skill growth. The R5 is the starting point for serious sim racers, not a ceiling.

olist: Define your time commitment. Five hours per week casual use suits Logitech. Ten hours weekly with intent to improve suits MOZA.
List other games or platforms you plan to race on. Logitech wins if you want console play or titles outside iRacing.
Check your cockpit and desk space. Direct-drive wheels run warm and need airflow; belt-drive wheels do not care.
Decide on budget for pedals now. MOZA R5 includes them; Logitech does not, so compare true total cost.

sections.p: Both wheels will carry you through your first season in iRacing comfortably. The real difference emerges in year two: the Logitech remains stable and dependable, while the MOZA invites you to build outward and climb through higher-level competitive series. Neither choice locks you in forever, but the MOZA path costs less to extend.

faqs.q: Is belt-drive outdated compared to direct-drive?
faqs.a: No. Belt-drive is a mature technology that works reliably. It simply delivers feedback differently—softer and more filtered. Many casual racers and console players prefer it. Direct-drive is not superior in absolute terms; it is more demanding and more transparent, which suits different priorities.

faqs.q: Can I use the Logitech G Pro in other sim racing games?
faqs.a: Yes. The G Pro works in Assetto Corsa Competizione, rFactor 2, Sim1, Microsoft Flight Simulator, PlayStation racing titles, and many others. MOZA R5 works primarily in Windows-based sims and is best supported in iRacing, ACC, and rFactor 2.

faqs.q: Will the MOZA R5 feel too strong for a first week?
faqs.a: Stronger than a belt-drive wheel, yes. Too strong for everyone, no. Most drivers adapt within 3–7 days if they race 5+ hours during that period. Reducing in-game force feedback strength (usually to 70-85% of maximum) eases the transition without losing fidelity.

faqs.q: Which wheel can I upgrade later without throwing money away?
faqs.a: MOZA R5 ecosystem supports wheel swaps and pedal upgrades while keeping the base. Logitech G Pro locks you into the Logitech ecosystem; upgrading means replacing the entire base. For long-term growth, MOZA preserves your investment better.
